subject.title: Codex app-server client closes before long maintenance turn completes; Gateway restart also terminates active turn without graceful recovery

question: For Codex-backed turns interrupted by Gateway restart or app-server client close after possible side effects, should OpenClaw resume, synthesize a final status, or fail closed with restart-specific recovery guidance?
rationale: The remaining behavior crosses Codex transport semantics, replay safety, Gateway lifecycle, session recovery, and channel delivery, so code can only implement the policy after maintainers choose the desired user-visible recovery contract.

options.title: Design restart-aware recovery
options.body: Define a single cross-surface policy for Gateway-shutdown interruption, unexpected app-server close, safe resume, and final user-visible follow-up, then implement it with focused tests.

options.title: Limit to diagnostics and copy
options.body: Keep runtime behavior fail-closed but make messages and logs distinguish Gateway restart from unexpected app-server failure.

options.title: Wait for live reproduction
options.body: Keep the issue open under live-repro until a current-main run proves the remaining long-maintenance failure trigger.

recommendation.title: Design restart-aware recovery
recommendation.body: Define a single cross-surface policy for Gateway-shutdown interruption, unexpected app-server close, safe resume, and final user-visible follow-up, then implement it with focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the current bounded Codex app-server recovery policy and are best positioned to decide the replay-safety contract.
